# Valkur AI — full audit

> Audited 2026-09-07 against `Scripts/Gameplay/Enemies/`, `Scripts/Gameplay/World/Navigation/`,
> `StreamingAssets/FSM/*.json`, `StreamingAssets/Spawners/spawners_instances.json` and the
> 25 shipped `MonsterDefinition` assets. Every number below was read out of the shipped source
> and data, or measured live in Play Mode with 30–31 monsters on the field. Nothing is estimated.
>
> Supersedes `.github/HOSTILE_AI_AUDIT.md` (2026-09-06, 5.2 → 7.1), which covered hostile
> behaviour only. This one covers the whole AI surface: hostiles, allies, ambient NPCs, bosses,
> the authoring layer and the content that drives it.

**Overall: 6.6 / 10.**

The machinery is now genuinely good — measured at **0.105 ms/frame and 0 B/frame for 31
monsters**, with one acquisition rule, one movement seam, one retreat helper, one path
follower and a budgeted A\*. What it lacks is not architecture. It is that **the world contains
no fights** (six vendor respawners and one empty wave template are the entire placed spawner
set), and that **the first monsters ever to cast spells stand motionless for up to 12 seconds
per cast** — measured live, three at once, on the roster shipped yesterday.

## What is genuinely good

- **Measured, not asserted: the AI is free.** 31 live brains ticked 200× — **0.105 ms per
  frame for the whole population, 3.4 µs per monster, 0.6 % of a 60 fps budget** — and
  **0 bytes** allocated over 300 ticks × 30 monsters. The steady state is allocation-free.
  (Caveat: a state TRANSITION is still a `new XState()`, and a mostly-steady window under-counts
  those.)
- **The path budget is not close to binding.** With 11 chasers live the demand is 22
  searches/s against a supply of 240 (`maxSearchesPerFrame: 4` at 60 fps) — 9× headroom, and
  it would only bind at ~120 simultaneous chasers.
- **"Refused this frame" and "no path exists" are different answers**, and a follower told
  "no path" walks straight at the target — which for a refused-because-busy search would mean
  walking into the wall the path was routing around.
- **One acquisition rule.** `FSMPerception.TryAcquire` is the only spelling; `IdleState` used
  to ask `IsBlocked`, `PatrolState` `IsClear`, and only one checked the target was alive.
- **One movement seam.** `FSMComponents.SetVelocity` — stun forces zero, root forces zero,
  knockback yields entirely. Every state writes through it.
- **The coded half of the machine is DECLARED and census-tested.** `FSMBuiltInTransitions`
  mirrors every `ChangeState(new X())`, and `FSMBuiltInTransitionRegistryTests` reads the state
  class source and fails in BOTH directions. Adding a transition without declaring it is red.
- **The allowed-state whitelist is a structural guarantee, not a convention.** It is the only
  reason vendors cannot fight (no state class reads `stats.faction`), the reason a shout cannot
  recruit them, and the reason no pre-existing monster can dodge however it is tuned.
- **Every knob publishes only when authored.** An unset `aiTuning` field writes nothing, so
  `FSMTuning`'s default runs — which is what kept every monster byte-identical when the struct
  was introduced.

## Findings, worst first

### A. Casters are statues (score 2.5, and it is live right now)

`NPCCastState` suppresses movement and exits only when `SpellCaster.CurrentPhase` returns to
`Ready`. `Ready` is reached after `prepare + channel + the spell's own cooldownDuration`.
So the freeze is the spell's **entire cooldown**, computed from the shipped catalogue:

| spell | freeze | | spell | freeze |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `war_cry` | **20.00 s** | | `frost_nova` | 6.00 s |
| `curse_of_frailty` | **12.00 s** | | `void_lance` | 4.00 s |
| `leap_slam` | **12.00 s** | | `seeking_shard` | 3.00 s |
| `thunderclap` | **11.00 s** | | `darkball` | 1.70 s |
| `shadow_step` | 8.00 s | | `hostile_slash_dark` | 1.24 s |

Measured live, 31 monsters on the field: **9 in `NPCCastState`, every one at velocity 0.00,
worst 10.3 s and still counting** — three Dark Dwarfs frozen 9.15 s, 9.92 s and 10.26 s
simultaneously, all mid-`leap_slam`. `leap_slam` is a *movement* spell.

It was latent before yesterday: `barbol_cyan` was the only autocasting monster in the project's
history and it casts one spell, `iceball`. The Dark roster is the first data to expose it, and
it exposed it six times over.

Three separate defects, and the fix is different for each:

1. **The state waits for the wrong signal.** It should return to Chase/Attack when the spell's
   ACTION is over (`Channel` finished), not when the slot is off cooldown. The cooldown is a
   rate limit on the ability, not a duration for the caster.
2. **`NPCAutoCast` re-arms on its own `periodSeconds` (hard-coded to 3 in
   `EntitySetup.ConfigureMonsterAutoCast`) regardless of the spell's cooldown**, so the entry
   fires, gets refused, and the two clocks are unrelated to each other.
3. **The spell list I authored is wrong for an autocaster.** Cooldowns of 8–20 s were tuned for
   a player who keeps moving between casts. Until (1) is fixed, no monster should autocast
   anything above ~2 s.

### B. There are no fights (score 1.0)

`StreamingAssets/Spawners/spawners_instances.json` holds **7 records**: six vendor respawners
(`vendor_pavel_respawn_5m` and friends) and one `survival_10`, whose template's `waves` array
is **empty**. Nothing else spawns hostiles: the dungeon room enemy spawner exists only inside
`World/Dungeon/Udemy/` and has no caller outside it (grep: zero).

So the entire AI layer — 8,311 lines, 21 dimensions below — is driven in normal play by
nothing at all. Every monster this audit measured had to be summoned from the console. That is
why this axis, not any behaviour gap, is the cheapest large win available: a dozen authored
spawners would do more for how the game feels than any item in section C.

The Dark roster is the same story one level down: six new hostiles, in the catalog, reachable
from the Entities editor and the `spawn` command, and placed **nowhere**.

### C. Behaviour gaps

1. **No threat model at all** (score 3.0). `FactionTargeting.EnemyOf` returns the NEAREST
   candidate, recomputed every frame. Consequences: damage buys no aggro, so a summon that
   tanks and a player who nukes are equally interesting; there is no hysteresis, so two
   candidates at similar distance make a monster's target flip frame to frame; and no monster
   can be taunted, peeled or pulled. Adding a per-machine "who hurt me, weighted, decaying"
   table is the single highest-leverage behaviour change left.
2. **Only ONE of three acquisition sites shouts.** `AggroBroadcast.Alert` has exactly one
   caller — `IdleState`. A monster that spots the player while **patrolling** (`PatrolState`,
   line 46) or while **searching** (`SearchState`, line 74) alerts nobody. Half the pack's
   perception is therefore private, and which half depends on where each monster happened to
   be in its patrol loop.
3. **`stats.faction` still reaches no AI decision.** It is authored on all 25 definitions and
   read by exactly three places: the loot roll, the respawn system, and one `SetContext` whose
   value nothing consumes. Allegiance is decided by `AlliedUnit` membership and by the FSM
   set's whitelist. That works, but the field reads like a promise it does not keep — the
   `animation_map.json` shape this project has documented a dozen times.
4. **Coordination is one shout and nothing else.** No roles, no flanking, no surround, no
   ranged/melee split, no reinforcement. Twenty monsters converging still converge on the same
   point along the same line.
5. **`attackVariants` is still authored on 5 of 18 hostiles** — `knight_red` plus the five dark
   twins that inherited theirs from the player classes. The other thirteen take the single
   attack set. That is art, not code.
6. **Difficulty does not scale** (score 2.0). `MonsterDefinition.GetScaledStats` moves hp, and
   derives meleeDamage/defense from hp's ratio — but `level` is **1 on every shipped asset** and
   nothing in the run raises it. There is no zone difficulty, no depth scaling, no elite roll.

### D. Newly introduced debt (yesterday's Dark roster)

1. **25 `castVariants` are inert on the monster side.** The dark twins inherited 3–9 cast
   animations each from their player classes, and `FSMMonsterBrain.OnFSMStateChanged` /
   `NPCCastState` both call the two-argument `SetState(state, direction)`, which REUSES the
   active variant index — and on a monster that index is never set, so it is −1 forever. Every
   dark caster plays the base cast pose, and `CastVariant.spellKeys` reservations never apply.
   Authored, round-tripped, inert. The fix is one call: resolve the variant from the spell key
   the way `PlayerController.ResolveCastVariant` already does.
2. **Six hostiles author `useAttackTelegraph` with spells that outrun it.** The telegraph is
   drawn on the melee windup; the spell path has no tell at all, so a `void_lance` arrives with
   no warning from a monster the player has learned always telegraphs.
3. **The dodge reaches 6 of 25 monsters** by design (two gates, both deliberate), which is
   correct for a first roster and means the axis cannot score above ~7 until a pre-existing
   hostile earns it.

### E. Engineering debt

1. **A state transition allocates.** `new XState()` per transition, plus the `new
   FSMComponents(...)` and `HashSet` at brain init. Measured steady-state alloc is 0 B/frame,
   so this only shows up in a churn-heavy fight.
2. **`PathFinder._walkCache` grows unbounded for the session** — noted in the previous audit,
   still true.
3. **No PlayMode test touches the AI at all**, and `NPCSeparationSystem` has no fixture in
   either mode (grep: zero files). Both are exactly the layers whose failure needs physics.
4. **`AIDebugOverlay` draws perception, not decisions.** Aggro ring, view cone, leash ring and
   the line to the target — but not the live path, not the dodge heading, not the sensed
   projectile, not the standoff band. The three newest behaviours are the three invisible ones.

## Suggested order of work

1. **Fix the cast freeze** (finding A). Exit `NPCCastState` when the channel ends, keep the
   cooldown as the ability's rate limit, and let `NPCAutoCast` respect the spell's own cooldown
   instead of a hard-coded 3 s. Then re-tune the six dark spell lists. One change, and it moves
   axes 4, 7, 9 and 12 at once — every caster in the game is currently a statue.
2. **Author encounters** (finding B). A dozen spawner placements is hours of work and it is the
   difference between an AI that exists and an AI the player meets.
3. **A threat table** (C1). Per-machine, damage-weighted, decaying, with hysteresis on target
   switch. Everything about roles, taunts and pet tanking is downstream of it.
4. **Shout from `PatrolState` and `SearchState`** (C2). Three lines; the pack currently shares
   perception only when it happens to be standing still.
5. **Resolve the cast variant from the spell key** (D1). Twenty-five authored animations are one
   call away from rendering.
6. Difficulty scaling by zone or depth (C6), and a PlayMode fixture over separation + a real
   chase (E3).

## Two traps worth keeping

- **Measure the WORK, not the clock, under `execute_code`.** `Time.deltaTime` reads ~0.0016
  there because nothing is rendering, so any per-frame timing derived from it measures the
  harness. The FSM cost above came from a `Stopwatch` around N explicit ticks, and the path
  budget verdict came from arithmetic (22 demanded vs 240 supplied) that no timing can distort.
- **A behaviour that is latent in the data is not a behaviour that works.** `NPCCastState` had
  shipped for the life of the project and the freeze was invisible, because exactly one monster
  autocast and it cast one 1.7 s spell. The defect was in the interaction between a state and a
  data range no shipped asset occupied — the same shape as the spawner coordinate drift, where
  both halves were internally consistent and only the composition was wrong.

body was measured on.

**Overall: 6.6 becomes 8.0.**

### The changes

1. **The cast freeze.** `NPCCastState` exits when the spell leaves `Prepare`/`Channel` instead
   of when the slot leaves `Cooldown`, with a clamped pose floor (0.30–0.85 s) taken from the
   entity's own cast animation so an instant spell still reads. `EntitySetup` derives each
   auto-cast entry's period from the spell's own `cooldownDuration` and its distance gate from
   the spell's `range`, replacing a hard-coded 3 s unrelated to either. Measured on the same
   28–31 monster load: **1–2 in the state at a worst of 0.83 s, 15 monsters moving, 6
   attacking** — against 9 frozen at 10.3 s before.
2. **Encounters.** Eight new templates, deliberately MIXED — a caster behind two melee is the
   composition `desiredRange`, the shout, the threat table and the ring were all built for.
   Ten placements across `Forest` and `zone_100_50`, and `survival_10`'s empty wave list
   replaced with ten waves / 40 monsters that escalate in SHAPE as well as number. All ten new
   placements verified live against real building and world colliders: **10/10 clear**. Three
   PRE-EXISTING placements are not — `survival_10` and two vendor respawns sit on a collision
   tile; left alone as out of scope, recorded here.
3. **Difficulty.** `EncounterDifficulty` resolves a level from the encounter's `levelBonus`
   (place) and `scaleWithPlayerLevel` (progress); `SpawnLevel` carries it on the spawned object
   so the two independent stat-scaling sites cannot disagree, and so nothing writes to the
   shared `MonsterDefinition`. Growth is PROPORTIONAL (`levelHpGrowth`) because the bestiary
   spans 10 to 10,000 hp and no absolute curve serves both ends. Measured: `barbol_baby`
   10 to 15 hp at L5, `barbol_gigante` 10,000 to 14,800, `dark_vampire` 240 to 442 at L8,
   vendors unchanged.
4. **Threat.** `ThreatMemory` plus `Health.OnDamagedBy`. Damage-weighted, half-life decay (8 s),
   a 1.35x switch margin so the target cannot oscillate, a range limit so one shot from a
   rooftop cannot own a monster, and a faction re-check so friendly splash never turns a
   monster on its own side.
5. **Faction.** `EntityFaction` derives a side from `AlliedUnit` membership, then the player
   registry, then the player tag, then the authored string. Neutrals are now unfightable and
   unfighting BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by their aggro range happening to be zero — and an
   ally no longer walks across town to kill the blacksmith.
6. **Surround.** `EngagementRing` gives each attacker an angular slot, so a pack encircles
   rather than queueing down one bearing. Measured live: occupancy 4 on the player.
7. **Hearing.** `NoiseEvents` on every melee swing and every cast — the single seams both pass
   through. Verified live: a player's spell alerts 2 nearby resting hostiles; the same noise
   made BY a hostile alerts 0 of its own side; neutrals hold no alerts, ever.
8. **Two animation defects found while fixing the above.** `DodgeState` was missing from
   `FSMMonsterBrain`'s state-to-animation switch, so the sidestep fell through to `_ => Idle`
   and rendered as a monster standing still while sliding sideways. And monsters never resolved
   a cast variant, so the 25 cast animations the Dark roster inherited from the player classes
   were unreachable.

### Still open

- **Bosses (5.5)** — one boss, no adds, no phase-specific behaviour.
- **Ambient NPC life (6.0)** — `StrollState` and `NPC_Passive` are two behaviours for seven
  characters; no schedules, no day/night routine, no reaction to weather.
- **`attackVariants` on thirteen hostiles** — needs art, not code.
- **Three pre-existing spawner placements sit on collision tiles** (see item 2).

### Closed in a second pass, same day

- **PlayMode coverage of the AI, which did not exist at all.** `HostileAiPlayTests` (6) and
  `NPCSeparationPlayTests` (4) — 10/10 green. They assert over ELAPSED TIME with the real loop
  running, which is the only shape that could have caught the cast freeze: every unit test of
  `NPCCastState` passed throughout its life, because each asserted the transition it was written
  for and none asked how LONG the monster stood there. `ACasterDoesNotSpendTheFightRooted` and
  `AMonsterNeverStopsMovingForeverWhileItHasATarget` are the regression guards.
- **`NPCSeparationSystem`'s first fixture in either mode.** It runs in `FixedUpdate`, reads
  collider radii off live entities and writes through the same body the FSM states write, so an
  EditMode test would have had to call its private step and would have measured the arithmetic
  rather than the thing that breaks.
- **`PathFinder._walkCache` is bounded.** It had no ceiling and `InvalidateWalkability` fires on
  a collision REBAKE, not on movement — so a streaming world grew the dictionary for the length
  of the session. Dropped wholesale at 65,536 cells rather than evicting least-recently-used:
  every value is a pure function of the collision world, so there is nothing to lose and no
  correctness question, where an LRU would need a second structure and a touch on every read on
  the solver's hottest path.
- **Two hot paths tightened.** `NoiseEvents` tests DISTANCE before allegiance (the side test is
  two `GetComponent` calls and the range test is a subtraction, and a noise is emitted on every
  swing); `ThreatMemory` caches each attacker's `Health` at record time instead of resolving it
  per entry per read, on a method every engaged monster reaches at least once a frame.

### A trap this second pass added

- **`yield return null` counts FRAMES, and the PlayMode runner is not capped to 60.** The first
  version of these fixtures waited 120 frames "for about two seconds", got roughly half a second
  of simulated time, and reported a monster correctly chasing at 4 u/s as having moved 0.96
  units — three red tests, every number real, none of them about the AI. Proved by driving the
  same `ChaseState` by hand through `execute_code`, which asked for exactly 4.00 u/s on every
  tick. Wait on `Time.time` for anything driven from `Update`, and on `WaitForFixedUpdate` for
  anything driven from `FixedUpdate`.

### Traps this pass added to the pile

- **A green console and a successful `refresh_unity` are still not proof an edit compiled.**
  Measured twice here: `mode=force, scope=all` returned `resulting_state: "idle"` and rebuilt
  nothing, while reflection reported the type as present because the STALE build also defined
  it. What forces it is `AssetDatabase.ImportAsset(path, ForceUpdate|ForceSynchronousImport)`
  followed by `CompilationPipeline.RequestScriptCompilation()`; what DETECTS it is a timestamp
  comparison per assembly against the newest `.cs` under that assembly's own tree — comparing
  against all of `Assets/` reports a false positive every time any test file is touched.
- **A test that ticks a fixed number of frames measures the state it lands in, not the exit
  under test.** Three fixtures here asserted on `ChaseState` and got `PatrolState`, because the
  ticks kept running after the transition and Chase correctly dropped to Patrol against a
  fixture target with no `Health`. Tick until the state changes, not a fixed count.
- **`AlliedUnit` joins its registry from `Awake`/`OnEnable`, and EditMode runs neither.** A bare
  `AddComponent<AlliedUnit>()` leaves `AlliedUnit.Live` empty, so a test measures the
  no-allies fast path and passes for the wrong reason. `SetLifetime` is the documented path
  that registers explicitly.
